title: Coca Room crowds and Blue Room dedications
summary: Photographs of crowds and Pork Chops and Kidney Stew, and Riddick's remark that the band could not take dedications.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Now this is at the... What a crowd. Yeah, this is at the coca room in the auditorium during one of our deals. See pork chops? Yeah. Kidney stew? They were...
Did they mostly sing or were they mostly comedy? What?
Just dance. Danced. With humble apologies to a great pianist from a bum guitar player, sincerely, Edmund Sushon. Huh. One of the finest men I ever knew.
Why did he send you that?

I have no idea unless it was in that thing, the second line that I showed you. This is Blaise D'Antoni's little child, Donna. She went into Hollywood and became a movie star. Oh, I remember that. Yeah. Donna D'Antoni. Sidney Gonzalez, Jr. I don't know. I don't know. I don't remember him. Did you please play something specially for me? For Mr. George Montagnet. Montagnet. M-O-N-T-A-G-N-E-T. Who is in our party. Thanks, Sid Gonzalez. That was at the Blue Room. We could not dedicate any numbers to anyone because if we had done that, we would have dedicated more than we would have played because that's the way people are. They want their name. I don't know where this is. At the Kappa Records in Hollywood. Yeah. This is at the, oh I don't remember. It was someplace where we played.
